idiom_name: tracing-subscriber Layer (or a log implementation) chaining hmac/sha2
implementation_notes: Rust's standard library has neither a logger nor a hash, so the idiom is a facade plus crates: implement tracing_subscriber::layer::Layer::on_event - or a log::Log impl when the facade must stay minimal - and chain an Hmac<Sha256> over prev || seq || canonical record, writing through an append-only sink. The hand-written path stays justified for a no_std or panic-path writer, and the log crate remains the right choice when the process must not depend on tracing's subsystem machinery.
pitfalls: Layer callbacks take &self, so the chain state must sit behind a Mutex/RefCell or a channel - the compiler will not let you keep it as a plain mutable field, and that is a feature, not an obstacle.
on_event runs on the emitting thread; holding the state lock across a blocking fsync serialises the whole application, so hand tagged bytes to one writer thread once throughput matters.

Canonicalisation must be derived from the structured fields, not from tracing's formatted output: field order follows the call site, and a verifier that re-parses Display text will disagree eventually.
